subject: Latency anomaly after model12x rollout — request for SLA relief and fallback
messages:
From: Ava Li <ava.li@brightpath.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@brightpath.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Latency & error spike after model12x rollout (prod)

Hi Redwood support,

We started receiving user reports and internal alerts ~08:50 PDT after the model12x production switch that went live at 08:30. p95 is fine but p99 and tail latency jumped ~6x and a subset of requests are returning 504s. This is impacting BrightPath search autosuggest and causes visible product regressions.

Short facts:
- Model variant deployed: model12x-2026-06-24 (quantized, variant A)
- Observed: p99 latency spike from ~420ms -> ~2.4s, 504 rate ~1.6% over a 15m window
- Affected routes: /api/v1/suggest (heavy short-sequence traffic)
- PID traces and per-token logs attached (brightpath_logs_20260625.zip)

Can you confirm whether this is a known regression for this build? We need an immediate mitigation plan and will require timeline for rollback or traffic steering. We are sensitive to SLA credits as this will impact our 99.9% availability target.

Thanks,
Ava Li
Head of Engineering, BrightPath
---
BrightPath | ava.li@brightpath.com

From: Redwood Support <support@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Li <ava.li@brightpath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency & error spike after model12x rollout (prod)

Hi Ava — thanks for the report and the logs. We've triaged the traces and see the same tail behavior on our side. Early signal points to an attention-kernel micro-behavior when sequence length < 32 for this quantized variant; we are validating now. Ben from account is looped in for next steps.

Immediate ask: can BrightPath tolerate a brief traffic cutover to a stable variant (model12x-vstable-2026-05-10) for the /api/v1/suggest route while we investigate? That variant has been used in canary previously and doesn't show the tail behavior.

We received your attachment: brightpath_logs_20260625.zip — saving to the case. We'll update within 30 minutes with mitigation plan.

— Redwood Support
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightPath latency — request for SLA relief + rollback authorization

Team — forwarding the BrightPath report. Impact looks real and customer is already flagging SLA exposure (99.9% 99th/99.9% uptime target). Support's initial repro points at the quantized variant.

Customer asks:
- Immediate mitigation (fallback to model12x-vstable-2026-05-10)
- Temporary SLA carveout while rollback is exercised and for the remediation window (they asked about credits)

My recommendation: authorize traffic switch for /api/v1/suggest to the stable variant, for a maximum of 3 hours, with communication to BrightPath. We should pre-authorize a limited SLA relief window tied to remediation — up to 6 hours of rolling window for evaluation before escalation to finance for credits.

Requesting decision from Marissa on SLA carveout and formal sign-off for traffic rollback.

Thanks, Ben
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightPath latency — request for SLA relief + rollback authorization

Marissa — quick technical summary: support ran a differential trace (attached model12x_vs_vstable_traces.csv) and confirmed that the quantized kernel path exhibits a 5–7x amplification of per-step overhead for very short sequences under heavy concurrency. There are two mitigation paths:

1) Traffic switch to model12x-vstable-2026-05-10 (no code change, immediate) — expected to restore tail latency to baseline within our routing propagation window (~90s).
2) Keep current variant and enable per-request serialization to thin the concurrency (software mitigation) — will take ~6–8 hours to validate and deploy safely.

Given customer impact on user-facing suggest, option 1 is low risk and fast. However, because this is a customer under an SLA we should document an explicit carveout: a temporary SLA-relief window (start timestamp, expected end, and rollback authorization) and a note that the fallback will be used only until a root-cause fix is validated. We should also capture that the regression is tied to quantization path for short sequences so we can prioritise a regression fix in the runtime team.

Can you approve a 3-hour immediate traffic switch and a 6-hour maximum SLA relief observation window (Ben suggested this), or do you prefer finance-led credit approvals?

— Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightPath latency — request for SLA relief + rollback authorization

On Thu, Jun 25, 2026 at 11:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Can you approve a 3-hour immediate traffic switch and a 6-hour maximum SLA relief observation window (Ben suggested this), or do you prefer finance-led credit approvals?

Approved:
- Authorize immediate traffic switch for /api/v1/suggest to model12x-vstable-2026-05-10.
- SLA relief: pre-authorize an observation window of up to 6 hours starting at the switch time. Any customer credit beyond behavior during that window must be escalated to Finance (cc: billing).
- Ask Support to confirm switch completion, collect post-switch metrics (p50/p95/p99, error-rate), and communicate to BrightPath with expected timeline and rollback confirmation.

Document expectations in the case: record model variants, timestamps, and attachments. Keep leadership (me) posted if remediation extends beyond the 6-hour window.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Li <ava.li@brightpath.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 15:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Action: traffic switch to stable variant completed — metrics & next steps

Ava — quick update from Redwood: per Marissa's sign-off we completed an automated traffic switch at 15:00 PDT to model12x-vstable-2026-05-10 for the /api/v1/suggest route. Highlights: 
- Switch completed at 2026-06-26T15:00:00-07:00 (routing propagation ~90s)
- Post-switch p99: 430ms (baseline ~420ms)
- 504/error rate: reduced to 0.02% in the 30m post-switch window

We have archived the logs and traces (model12x_vs_vstable_traces.csv) and set a 6-hour observation window per approved carveout. Support will continue root-cause analysis on the quantized kernel path and will follow up with a remediation ETA. If remediation requires an extended rollback beyond the 6-hour window, we'll escalate to Finance for credits per the SLA.

Attachments: model12x_vs_vstable_traces.csv

Thanks for working with us on this — please reply if you want us to keep the stable variant longer while we ship a fix.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Engineer, Runtime Reliability — Redwood Inference
